finding: the fix balances the instruction count across leading zeros and does not balance the cost
why:
First, containment. The earlier count was 42,633,192 instructions for a call the
paper measured at 5,535,140 ticks, and neither figure was what its name said: both
came from a driver passing a curve parameter where the library passes NULL, so both
described scalar multiplication on a different curve. Corrected, the call retires
about nine and a half million instructions in about 1.6 million ticks, a rate a wide
out-of-order core reaches. The impossible arithmetic is gone.
reading: One leading zero and sixty-three each SAVE almost the same number of instructions, while the measured time differs by nearly two orders of magnitude, which is why an instruction count cannot stand in for the cost here. delta_vs_256 is the 256-bit count minus the shorter class's, so a positive delta is a saving; an earlier revision of this field read it as an addition and the paper repeated the inverted sign.
method: callgrind at 100 and 200 calls per class, differenced, so process startup cancels; one nonce class per run with the scalar fixed
